outline.description: This chapter introduces the parties, the patents-in-suit, and the specific technology involved in the dispute, establishing the factual foundation necessary to understand the infringement allegations.
subtopics: Identification of Parties: Finesse Wireless LLC versus AT&T Mobility and Nokia
Overview of Asserted Patents: U.S. Patent Nos. 7,346,134 and 9,548,775
Technical Background: Passive Intermodulation (PIM) and Intermodulation Products (IMPs)
The Accused Product: Nokia Radios and PIM Cancellation Features
Trial Outcome: Jury Verdict of Infringement and $166 Million Damages Award

outline.chapter_title: Procedural Posture and Standards of Review
outline.description: This chapter outlines the procedural history leading to the appeal and details the specific legal standards the Federal Circuit applies when reviewing district court decisions on judgment as a matter of law and jury findings.
subtopics: District Court Proceedings: Denial of JMOL and New Trial Motions
Jurisdiction and Appellate Review Standards under 28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(1)
Standard of Review for JMOL Denials: Fifth Circuit Law Applied De Novo
Substantial Evidence Standard for Jury Findings of Infringement
Claim Construction Review Standards: De Novo and Clear Error

outline.description: This chapter examines the Federal Circuit's reasoning regarding the '134 patent, focusing on the sufficiency of expert testimony to prove the accused device sampled the required signals as claimed.
subtopics: Claim Limitation 1[a]: Requirement to Sample 'Signals of Interest' and 'Interference Generating Signals'
Expert Testimony Analysis: Dr. Wells' Mapping of Signals to RF ADC Inputs
The Timing Contradiction: Sampling Signals Generated Downstream
Evaluation of Conflicting Testimony and Lack of Substantial Evidence
Reversal of JMOL Denial for the '134 Patent Claims

outline.description: This chapter explores the court's analysis of the '775 patent, addressing issues of prosecution history estoppel regarding signal counts and the failure to prove the specific mathematical multiplications required by the claims.
subtopics: Claim Construction: Interpretation of 'Three Signals S1, S2, and S3'
Prosecution History Analysis: Rejection of Surrender of Claim Scope Argument
Claim Limitation 1[d]: Requirement for Seven Specific Multiplications
Evidence Deficiencies: Failure to Map Accused Device Operations to Claim Multiplications
Reversal of JMOL Denial for the '775 Patent Claims

outline.description: This chapter concludes the textbook explanation by covering the court's handling of the damages award and the final judgment, illustrating the dependency of damages on a valid infringement finding.
subtopics: Standard of Review for Denial of New Trial on Damages
Logical Dependency: Impact of Infringement Reversal on Damages
Decision to Vacate the Lump-Sum Damages Award
Final Judgment: Reversal and Vacation
Allocation of Costs to Defendants-Appellants
